cells.tense: The thinking is moving fast right now, and it is landing beside people rather than over them.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something this week with no plan and no case for it — the thing you want to try because it pulled at you. Let those close to you watch you want something, not reason your way toward it.
cells.core:
You find the shape of a problem quickly, and when you say it the air eases, because someone has finally said the thing plainly. That works best when the person beside you can still hear their own version of it after you finish. When they can, your speed opens something rather than closing it, and they stay in the conversation as themselves instead of as a listener.

There is a pleasure in beginning before you know where a thing is going — not the plan, the first motion. You do not need a reason for it yet. Starting for the pull of starting gives the quick mind a place to go that belongs to you, and the ones near you get to see you want something instead of only watch you work it out.
cells.sheetLine: You see it fast — say it so they can still hear themselves.
cells.verb: cutting through to what is actually true, fast
cells.place: where you feel with people and stay aligned with them

cells.tense: It will already be decided before the other person has finished saying what they meant.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Take one decision you have been making on someone else's behalf and hand it back — say where your part ends, then let that space stand without stepping in to speed it up.
cells.core:
Here the fast mind runs ahead of whoever it is with. You have the answer while they are still finding the sentence, and the face across from you starts to feel like an audience instead of a partner. The point was to spare them the slow part. What happens instead is that they stop arriving on their own, and the closeness you are after goes thin.

There is a clear thing you have been carrying that was not only yours. Say where you stop and they begin, and mean it — then let that space stay even when you could fill it faster. The line is not against the person. It is around the part of the decision that belongs to you. Holding it is what lets them come back in as themselves instead of as someone agreeing with you.

cells.tense: It saw the true shape of things, and the door it stood at is already behind it.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Pick one person you know and ask what something has honestly been like for them — the feeling under the story, not the story — and keep following whatever comes, for as long as it keeps coming.
cells.core:
The clarity is there. What is missing is the room it was meant for. You can see how a thing works and where it will land, and you have not been bringing that into anything that matters, so those who know you get the easy version and the connection the sight was for goes unused. Wondering with someone what a thing means to them has gone quiet. It is not gone.

One other person and one honest question is enough to start it moving again. Ask someone you know what a thing has really been like for them, and stay with the answer instead of refining it. You are not there to solve it. You are there to mean what you say beside them for a few turns, and to let them mean what they say back. The understanding moves once it is shared rather than kept.

cells.tense: You keep people close by hearing what something means under what they said, and by your own account you were only passing through.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: With whoever comes to you next with something that matters, stay in what they feel and mend nothing — no summary, no answer, no label for what you think is there.
cells.core:
People open up near you, and the air stays level, and if anyone asked how that happened you would say the two of them just get along. What they get along on is you — the reading of what sits under the words, the small adjustments nobody sees. You have been holding bonds together well enough to have convinced yourself you were holding nothing.

Stay with the next thing someone brings you and mend nothing. Hear what they feel, and then let it be — no tidying, no moving the conversation on, no label for what you think is there. The longer you sit with what they said, the more you notice it is yours too, and the work you have been doing and your own part in it come back into the same frame. Nothing else has to change for that to be enough.
